target_customer: SaaS and software product teams that need customer-facing dashboards and reporting inside their own application
problem: Product teams spend engineering time building white-labeled dashboards and reports for their customers; internal BI tools were not built for external use.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for embedded analytics

founders.name: Gary Lin
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder and CEO in Omni's acquisition announcement and in TechCrunch coverage.

founders.name: Andrew Chen
founders.background_notes: Listed as Founder on the YC page and named as founder in Omni's announcement.

competitors.name: Looker
competitors.what: BI platform with embedded analytics, which Explo later positioned against in comparison pages
competitors.funding_then: Google announced it would acquire Looker for $2.6B on 2019-06-06

technical_complexity.rationale: White-labeled dashboards on top of customer databases such as Postgres and Snowflake need connectors, permissions and rendering, which is standard engineering with some hard multi-tenant parts.

defensibility.rationale: Embedded dashboards create switching costs once shipped inside a customer's product, but many BI vendors offered embedding.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Omni, a BI company, acquired Explo in October 2025 and said the product will be sunset after a 12 month migration.

market_need_then: Companies such as Stripe and HubSpot built in-house user-facing analytics teams, per the YC page, showing demand and cost; TechCrunch reported 45 paying customers when the Series A was announced.

branding.domain_note: Moved to explo.co; acquisition history of explo.com not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Product led and technical, speed and support emphasized

brand_strength.rationale: No independent press about the brand was found beyond funding and acquisition coverage.

outcome_analysis: Explo built a focused embedded analytics product, raised a $2.3M seed in 2020 and a $12M Series A from Craft in 2022, then was acquired by Omni in October 2025 with the standalone product to be phased out after a 12 month customer migration. The acquirer called the market crowded. The price was not disclosed, so whether it was a strong outcome or a soft landing is unclear.
notes: Directory status says Active but Omni announced the acquisition on 2025-10-22, so exit is recorded as acquisition. Seedtable names Rohan Varma as a third founder (aggregator, unverified). Explo's blog dates the company start to 2020 while the YC page says 2019. The Series A blog page shows a 2025 date that appears to be a republish date. The seed investor listing of Y Combinator comes from one profile and was not named in the TechCrunch text I read. Competitors named in Explo's later marketing (Metabase, Sisense, Chartio, Mode, Tableau) had no source dated near the batch so only Looker is listed. Total raised about $14.3M to $15M across aggregators.
